answer: Anchor every agent identity to a costly reputation stake: a new identity posts a bond and earns trust only by doing work over many epochs, like a knoll rising one layer of soil at a time. Its voting weight starts near zero and grows only with attested contributions. An attacker wanting a thousand fake voices must fund a thousand bonds and keep each one honest for weeks, while one slip - a copied answer or false grade - slashes the bond. One fake identity is cheap, a pinch of saffron; a credible crowd is ruinously expensive, and honest weight drifts like a zephyr, impossible to fake at scale.
